name: Topological Sort
description: Topological sort orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) so that for every directed edge u → v, u comes before v. It is used wherever there are dependencies: course prerequisites, build systems, and task scheduling.
approach: Kahn's algorithm: compute in-degrees, enqueue all zero-in-degree nodes, repeatedly dequeue, append to order, and decrement in-degrees of neighbors, enqueuing any that hit zero. If the output has fewer nodes than V, a cycle exists. DFS-based: mark visited and append nodes in post-order, then reverse.
use_cases: Determining build order of tasks with prerequisites.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to detect that a cycle means no valid topological order exists.
Using the DFS post-order list without reversing it.
